name: Seated Tibialis Raise with Band
description: A seated exercise targeting the tibialis anterior through dorsiflexion against resistance from a band. The exerciser sits with one end of a resistance band looped around the forefoot, with the other end anchored forward. By pulling the toes back toward the shin against band resistance, the tibialis anterior — the muscle running along the outer shin — is loaded. This exercise is critical for shin splint prevention, anterior compartment syndrome rehabilitation, and ankle stability programs.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the floor or a chair with the leg extended forward. Loop a resistance band around the forefoot, anchoring the other end to a stable object in front of the foot. Begin with the foot in a neutral or slightly plantarflexed position.
execution.setup_instructions: Anchor the band to something at floor level — a heavy dumbbell, power rack base, or a door anchor near the floor. The band should provide resistance against dorsiflexion (pulling toes up).
steps: Step 1: Sit with the leg extended and the band looped around the top of the foot, anchored in front.
Step 2: Pull the toes and forefoot back toward the shin (dorsiflexion) against the band resistance.
Step 3: Hold the dorsiflexed position briefly, feeling the contraction along the outer shin.
Step 4: Slowly lower the foot back toward the starting position under control. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you dorsiflex (pull toes back). Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Using the entire leg to assist the movement — only the foot should move
Not achieving full dorsiflexion range due to band tension that is too heavy
Allowing the heel to lift from the floor, reducing tibialis anterior isolation
safety_considerations: This exercise should be pain-free in both directions — if pulling back causes sharp shin pain, reduce band tension
For shin splint rehab: start with lighter band and higher reps, progress gradually
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full dorsiflexion — toes pull back as far as the ankle allows without the leg lifting from the floor.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2s dorsiflexion, 1s hold, 3s slow return (the eccentric return is critical for shin splint rehab)
coaching_cues: Feel the muscles along the outer shin working — that is the tibialis anterior
Slow on the way down — the controlled lowering phase builds the most strength for shin splint prevention
Keep the heel grounded throughout the movement
